one_liner: Copper CRM has a documented REST Developer API using API keys, available through a 14-day free trial or a paid plan; OAuth2 requires contacting Copper to register an app; no official MCP confirmed by the provided pages.
auth_notes: API key is sent via X-PW-AccessToken, X-PW-Application and X-PW-UserEmail headers. Only Admin users can generate keys, and keys carry no scopes. OAuth2 exists but the application must first be registered by contacting Copper, so API key is the practical self-serve method. developer.copper.co is a different product and was ignored.
access_notes: Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial without a credit card, and the trial runs on the Business plan. No free plan is shown in the pages. The pages say API access needs a plan that includes it, but they do not list which paid plans include it. The draft claim that Basic has no API is not backed by the pages.
blocker_notes: The API requires a trial or a paid plan that includes API access. Each customer must have an Admin generate a key. OAuth2 app registration requires contacting Copper.

evidence.quote: Copper offers both OAuth and API_KEY authentication modes. To use OAuth2.0 with Copper, you must first register your application.
Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial, and no credit card is required.
During your free trial, you will be using our CRM software on the Business plan to experience the full capabilities of Copper.
You need a Copper account on a plan that includes API access.
The Copper Developer API ("Dev API") provides a RESTful interface with JSON-formatted responses to access most Copper resources.
an API is available for custom integrations
